concepts.quote: With %.3f it would print 3.142 and no spaces. price itself is still 3.14159; only the printed digits change.
concepts.why: Correctly predicts the effect of changing the precision to .3 (3.14159 rounds to 3.142, no width so no padding) and states that only the printed digits change, not the stored value, matching the L4 predict_a_change way; it does not, however, answer the asked part about the given %6.2f and %d output.

Makes one correct programming-specific statement that the double variable keeps its stored value and is unaffected by formatted printing, but says nothing more about double arithmetic, representation or type flow.
